confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds on Study 3 alone: 198 people analyzed across four randomized arms, with about 100 people in each phase group.

Paper inconsistency that changes no form value: the text says 35% of Study 1 interviewees held master's degrees or above, but Appendix A lists 7 master's and 1 doctorate (8 of 20, 40%). The form does not record this share.

summary: The PDF supports every participant count in the c067 form: Study 3 analyzes 198 of 205 recruited employees (7 failed attention checks), Studies 2a and 2b analyze 42 and 44 students who each worked in both conditions, Study 1 interviews 20 people, and the paper prints no count at assignment or by arm, so the null counts are right. Criterion 2 holds on Study 3 alone (198 people in four randomized arms, about 100 per phase), and the gaps the check found (no Study 3 cell sizes, no statement on Study 1 versus Study 3 overlap) change no count.
